topics.label: Introduction to the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's learning outcomes and outlines the framework of cancer hallmarks across tumor progression.

topics.label: Growth signal independence and signaling pathway deregulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in receptor tyrosine kinases, Wnt/beta-catenin, and downstream cascades drive autonomous cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Block to terminal cell differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells fail to withdraw from the cell cycle and differentiate into mature functional cell types in hematological malignancies and colorectal carcinoma.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how alterations in p53 and Bcl-2 family proteins prevent mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization and apoptosis in cancer cells.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and p53 genome protection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how telomere dynamics and stress signals induce senescence via p53, how cancer cells bypass these barriers, and synthesize these cell-autonomous growth hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the Warburg effect, tissue-specific metabolic rewiring, and mutations in Krebs cycle enzymes that produce epigenetic-altering oncometabolites.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the physiological requirement, timing, and molecular balance of angiogenic signaling necessary to sustain tumor growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms, monitoring, and genetics of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the metastatic cascade, seed-and-soil interactions, liquid biopsy tracking using circulating tumor cells, and genomic patterns such as whole-genome duplication.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer summarizes the core themes of cancer hallmarks, discusses recent literature expansions, and provides concluding framing for the lecture.
